title: Find the Pivot Integer
summary: Determine the pivot integer x for a given positive integer n, where the sum of integers from 1 to x equals the sum of integers from x to n.
statement: Determine the pivot integer x for a given positive integer n, where the sum of integers from 1 to x equals the sum of integers from x to n. Return x if it exists, otherwise return -1. Ensure there is at most one such pivot index.
constraints: Find x from one through n such that 1+...+x equals x+...+n.
Return x when it exists, otherwise -1.
hints: Let T=n(n+1)/2 be the total sum.
Balancing inclusive sums gives x squared = T.
Take the integer square root of T and return it only when its square equals T.
The algebra is reversible, so a perfect-square triangular total is necessary and sufficient for an integer pivot.
editorial: The algebra is reversible, so a perfect-square triangular total is necessary and sufficient for an integer pivot.

tests.explanation: The sums one through six and six through eight both equal twenty-one, so the pivot is six.
No integer from one through four balances the two inclusive sums.
